remaining: Durable World binding resolution, cross-source claim display rules and legacy verb policy belong to later identity/verb work. Synthetic subscription crossing remains a named pending v2 gate. Live Herdr evidence requires HERDR_WORLD_LIVE_ADAPTERS=1 and the installed Herdr binary.

partialEvidence.review: The accepted delivery link records the merged design contract, not implementation acceptance. This adapter implementation awaits independent PR review.

evidenceDecision: P3 selects direct external-source conformance rather than a finite model. Existing runtime/snapshot models remain required for their unchanged owner fences; these tests establish the new adapter boundary, not durable identity, effect recovery or v2 delivery. Typed runtime-port translation and actual raw-client-free snapshot, Desk screen and terminal-setting consumers add direct compatibility evidence; native traffic, lease ownership and no-replay behavior retain their existing contracts. Remaining callback areas are explicitly TUI-only; no core runtime is enabled. Issue #1437 uses one shared runtime-reported foreground group leader basename check, ignoring arguments and children. The finite TUI/core input and World+SQLite answer matrices cover shell/REPL/editor/ssh, privilege/database and multiplexer/launcher refusals, child/MCP exclusion, resumed/restarted and arbitrary executable names, and pre-PR compatibility when foreground information is absent. No tty or /proc inspection is used for admission. Shell-exit checks at answer, dispatch and final preparation prove zero writes, Not sent, retrieval and no revival on both runtimes. Existing qualified runtime/terminal fences and opaque possible-send recovery remain unchanged; held-send cancellation uses the real framed transport. The stateless predicate adds no ordering state; finite class/path and preparation-boundary tests cover its decisions, while the full canonical gate retains ordering evidence. Outbox browser checks cover plain reasons, Copy answer and qualified draft-only recovery. A shell inside a live harness and runtimes without foreground information remain documented limits; no atomic OS foreground-and-send or live-platform guarantee is claimed. Follow-up #1447 covers Town/Board peek replies and review-feedback prefill: the shared request marker opts into that same final check, is stripped before native input, and leaves direct Terminal authority unchanged. Finite entry-point/foreground matrices cover submit, prefill and menu-key requests with stale/absent labels, admitted/refused leaders, retired generations and revoked browser authority. Real caller tests require the marker; desktop/phone browser recovery retains review drafts and copies the original compiled text without input or retry. These callers remain TUI-only where raw pane input was already supported; core native guard consumers remain unchanged. The opt-in adds no state or competing writer, so no new model is needed; existing runtime/effect ordering models and the full gate remain required.

promotion.scope: New adapter boundary only; independent implementation review and CI required.
